steps.title: Galets roulés
steps.body: Châteauneuf-du-Pape's most famous soil is covered with galets roulés, large, round quartzite stones left by the ancient Rhône. They store heat by day and release it at night, helping ripening, and protect the soil from drying. But Châteauneuf also has sand, which gives elegant wines like Château Rayas, and limestone.

steps.title: Thirteen grapes
steps.body: Châteauneuf allows 13 grape varieties, counted as 18 including colour variants: red, white and pink. Grenache usually dominates, often 70% or more. Château de Beaucastel famously uses all 13. Yields are low, about 35 hl/ha. Wines are rich, warm, spicy, with red fruit, garrigue herbs and leather, often 14.5 to 15.5% alcohol.

options: Large round stones that store heat
steps.explanation: These river stones warm the vines at night.

steps.title: Bottles and age
steps.body: Many Châteauneuf bottles carry the papal coat of arms embossed on the glass. Most of the wine is red; about 7% is white. Good Châteauneuf ages 10 to 20 years, gaining leather, game and dried fruit. Neighbouring Gigondas and Vacqueyras offer similar, often more affordable wines.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Galets roulés store heat in Châteauneuf's vineyards
Its rich, spicy reds age 10 to 20 years
